# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 28 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 28 | **Condition:** very fragmentary (final column)

---

**1** [...] I give You thanks, O Lord, for You have [...] with Your servant [...]

**2** [...] and You kept me going by Your mercy, and through the richness of [...]

**3** [...] Your compassion for everyone who seeks You honestly [...]

**4** [...] and You never abandoned the fatherless, and You never looked down on the weak [...]

**5** [...] because Your strength has no limits, and Your glory cannot be measured [...]

**6** [...] and amazing warriors serve You, and [...] the humble [...]

**7** [...] among those made clean in the dust of [...] Your servants [...]

**8** [...] You lifted up from the dust to sit in Your eternal council [...]

**9** [...] and You washed away the corruption of their spirit so they could stand [...]

**10** [...] in the ranks of the holy ones and join the fellowship [...]

**11** [...] of the heavenly assembly, and You gave them an everlasting inheritance [...]

**12** [...] and there is no one who can intervene to undo what You have done [...] or reverse [...]

**13** [...] Your fury, and there is no way back for those who [...] against You [...]

**14** [...] forever and ever. Amen and amen. [...]

**15** [...] Selah. [...]

---

*PNEUMA notes: Column 28 is the final surviving column of 1QHa, very fragmentary. The scroll's last words return to where it began: a thanksgiving to the God who lifts dust-creatures into the company of angels. The double "Amen" and "Selah" seal the entire collection as liturgical prayer. It is fitting that this scroll — found in Cave 1 at Qumran — ends with a word of worship rather than theology, devotion rather than doctrine.*
